newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nine women die in German psychiatric hospital fire.
newsitem.headline: Nine women die in German psychiatric hospital fire.

text.p: Nine elderly German women were killed in a fire that destroyed a dormitory in a psychiatric hospital in the small northern town of Rickling, police said on Monday.
The women, aged between 55 and 85, were psychiatric patients at the hospital. Police said they did not yet know the cause of the fire, but said arson could not be ruled out.
The fire broke out late on Sunday. Initial reports said only two people had been killed in the blaze.
But police said seven further bodies were discovered on Monday in the smouldering remains of a building where the patients lived.
They said that 23 people who lived in the wooden building were evacuated on Sunday night without injury. Authorities were at first unsure how many patients were in the building when the fire started.
"The corpses of the seven elderly women were found in the ruins on the day after the fire," said Peter Sutter, a spokesman for Innere Mission, which operated the hospital.
Rickling is about 40 km (25 miles) north of Hamburg and a similar distance east of Luebeck, where 10 people were killed in a fire last January at a foreigners' hostel in Germany.

Although it was initially feared the Luebeck fire was started by neo-Nazis, state prosecutors later said the fire was started by a Lebanese man who lived in the house. He is on trial charged with aggravated arson and causing bodily harm.
